# Hypersleep [italic]From ColonyPedia, the free encyclopedia of the frontier. For the Chroma Sleep song, see Hypersleep Heart.[/italic]
[bold]Hypersleep[/bold], also called cryosleep, the long nap or the tube, is a state of suspended animation used for journeys between star systems. A sleeper's body is cooled and slowed until it barely ages, so that a crew can cross months or years of travel without eating, drinking or going mad.
## HISTORY Hypersleep chambers were made practical in the early twenty-second century. Early models were known for the Wake Shakes, a full body tremble lasting up to a day, and for the dreams, which sleepers are not supposed to have. Modern pods from Weyland-Yutani and Seegson reduce the Shakes to an hour. Sleepers still report dreams (citation needed).
## EFFECTS ON THE BODY - [bold]Ageing.[/bold] A sleeper ages around one day for every month asleep. Opinions differ, and the actuaries are not saying. - [bold]Waking.[/bold] Nausea, cold, confusion and an urge to tell everyone about the dream. Crews are advised to eat something salty and not to tell everyone about the dream. - [bold]Long term.[/bold] Repeat sleepers may lose track of the date, their family and their own age, which can be a relief.
## SOCIAL EFFECTS Because news, mail and pay travel at the speed of the ship, a colonist returning from a long contract can find that their favourite band has broken up, reformed, and broken up again. ColonyPedia calls this relay lag. Colonists call it coming home.
## SAFETY Hypersleep is very safe. Most reported accidents involve pods opened early, pods opened late, or a pod opening on its own at the request of the ship's computer for reasons the ship's computer did not log. See also: Company Special Orders (article deleted).
